chunks: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: “If a man forgot to perform istinjāʾ after relieving himself until he prayed, he does not repeat the salat (prayer).”

So this is to be understood as referring to one who did not perform istinjāʾ with water, even if he had performed istinjāʾ with stones, or had not performed istinjāʾ with stones. But if he had performed istinjāʾ with water, then whenever he remembers that he had not performed istinjāʾ at all, repeating the salat (prayer) becomes obligatory upon him. That which indicates this is what he narrated:
As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā, who said:

key_terms.إِعَادَةُ: repetition, i.e. performing the salat (prayer) again
key_terms.الْغَائِطِ: defecation; the state requiring cleansing after relieving oneself
key_terms.بِالْأَحْجَارِ: with stones, indicating dry cleansing materials
key_terms.بِالْمَاءِ: with water, indicating purification by water
key_terms.رَوَاهُ: he narrated it, introducing the supporting report
key_terms.يَسْتَنْجِيَ: to perform istinjāʾ, cleansing oneself after relieving oneself

ai.seo_question: Does a person have to repeat salat (prayer) if he forgot istinjāʾ after relieving himself?
ai.summary: This text addresses a fiqh ruling concerning one who forgets istinjāʾ after defecation and then performs salat (prayer). It clarifies that the initial report is understood in a restricted sense, and that if one later remembers he had not purified himself at all, repeating the salat (prayer) is obligatory.
